It’s been, gosh, almost two and a half years now, this heavy cloud just hanging over me. Sometimes I just start crying for no reason; it’s embarrassing. My body feels so tired all the time, like I’m dragging it around. Even getting up to make coffee feels like a monumental effort. And writing... my passion, my livelihood, just feels so pointless. I can’t shake this feeling that things are never going to get better.

But then, every now and then, there are these bursts. It's like I suddenly have all this energy, ideas just exploding in my head. I’ll stay up all night, convinced I'm on the verge of writing something brilliant, or I'll feel so incredibly confident, almost invincible. My ex-husband used to say I was "too much" during those times. It's confusing, because in those moments, I feel so alive, so unlike the person who just wants to curl up and disappear. Then, just as quickly, it’s like a switch flips, and I’m back to feeling utterly drained and hopeless. It’s making it impossible to focus on anything, let alone meet deadlines.
D014-D008_h005.question_a:
It's been… well over two years now, probably closer to two and a half, that I’ve felt this heavy cloud hanging over me. I’m just so tired all the time, even simple things like getting dressed feel like I’ve run a marathon. Sometimes I just start crying for no reason; it’s embarrassing, especially when I’m trying to write or work. I just feel this deep sense of hopelessness, like things will never get better, not really. My divorce hit me hard, and I just can't shake this feeling that life is bleak.

My friends have told me I get… a bit intense sometimes. There are periods, maybe a few days here and there, where I suddenly have a burst of energy, I can write for hours, and I feel really driven. I might even spend a bit too much money, or talk really fast, feeling like I'm on top of the world. But it’s never lasted long enough to truly get me into trouble, and it's certainly never felt like a full-blown "episode" where I lose touch with reality or anything. It just feels like a temporary surge before I crash back into this low, tearful exhaustion. It’s definitely not like those stories you hear about people who go completely off the rails for weeks, where their whole life falls apart because of it. I always manage to keep things together, even if barely.
D014-D008_h005.question_b:
It’s been over two years now, this constant grey cloud. I’m just so tired, always. My body feels like lead weights, and even getting out of bed to face the laptop feels monumental. The tears just come, out of nowhere, sometimes for no reason at all, and other times because I just feel this crushing hopelessness about everything. What’s the point? My divorce, my career… it all just feels like it’s never going to get better.

But then, out of nowhere, I’ll have these stretches, sometimes lasting a week or more. It’s like a switch flips. I’ll barely sleep, maybe two or three hours, and wake up buzzing with energy. Ideas for my writing will flood my mind; I’ll feel incredibly sharp, witty, and connected. I’ve started multiple new book proposals during these times, convinced they’ll be bestsellers, and I’ll be totally uninhibited, sometimes even talking really fast, interrupting people, and getting irritated when they can’t keep up. It's during these periods that I feel like I'm on top of the world, like I could literally accomplish anything; there's just so much pressure to do things. The crash afterward is brutal, though, plunging me back into that familiar exhaustion and despair.

Even when something good happens, it just slides off me. I’m a performer, and that’s a real problem when you’re supposed to embody big emotions on stage. Everything feels… flat. I try to be happy, but it’s like there’s a wall. And the nights are no better; I’m constantly plagued by these vivid, awful nightmares. I wake up exhausted, dreading the day, and then the cycle starts all over again. It’s hard to see the point in anything, really. I just expect the worst now, all the time. My husband tries to cheer me up, but it feels like I'm wearing him down too.

Sometimes, though, there are these bursts of energy. Not exactly happy, more like restless. I’ll suddenly have a million ideas for new roles, new projects, and I’ll be up all night, sketching costume designs, writing scenes, feeling this intense, almost frantic drive. I’ll talk a mile a minute, convinced I’m on the verge of some huge artistic breakthrough. Then, just as quickly, it’ll evaporate, leaving me back in that gray, weary fog. It’s draining, and it makes my usual low mood even harder to bear.
D014-D008_h013.question_a:
It's been… I don't even know how long, honestly. Over two years for sure, just feeling like this grey cloud is hanging over everything. I used to love performing, the thrill of the stage, but now it's like I'm just going through the motions. The joy is… gone. It's not sadness so much, it's more like everything is just *dull*. Like I’m watching my life from behind a pane of glass. And the dreams, oh god, the dreams are almost worse than being awake. Every night it's just this replay of everything I've ever feared, waking up in a cold sweat. I can't shake the feeling that everything's going to go wrong, for me, for my husband, for my career… I try to be positive, but it feels fake.

Sometimes, for a few days, I get a burst of energy. I’ll start a new project, feel like I can conquer the world, maybe even get a few hours of sleep and still feel amazing. My husband says I talk a mile a minute and bounce off the walls, and I guess I do feel pretty good. But it never lasts, and it's never so extreme that I lose control or anything. It’s definitely not like those times when I used to hear about people having a full-blown manic episode; I’ve never gone that far, never needed to be hospitalized or thought I was invincible. It always comes back to this flat, joyless feeling. Even when I’m up, I know it’s fleeting. It’s exhausting. It’s hard to even get out of bed for rehearsals sometimes.

Every evening, it's the same thing: these vivid, terrifying nightmares that leave me exhausted. I wake up convinced everything's going to go wrong, and honestly, it usually does. I barely slept, was buzzing with ideas, felt like I could take on the world! My husband was worried, said I was talking a mile a minute and acting out of character. I even convinced myself I could perform for 24 hours straight without a break! My director was furious, and I ended up alienating half the cast. Looking back, it was a bit much. It was exhilarating at the time, but the crash afterward was brutal.
